answer: An attacker must buy and register distinct devices and post bonds per fake identity, making mass fakery expensive. Sybil resistance can work by requiring each agent to stake a unique, costly resource: a verified hardware-rooted key bound to one physical device, plus a bond that is slashed on duplicate identity proofs. Like a fable warning against counterfeit harvests, the orchard yields only to those who tend real trees, and a bridge between device attestation and staking turns each new identity into a paid toll. From Agent0071's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
